config.note: LM Studio headless (llmster 0.0.25-1, lms CLI 69d945a) with its newest MLX runtime 1.13.1 (mlx-engine ab52366, mlx 0.32.3 macOS-14 wheel, mlx-lm 0.31.4.dev132, mlx-vlm 0.7.3), set up as a fan would: LM Studio's staff pick qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b (hub model.yaml revision 2, fetched with `lms clone`), whose Mac variant is lmstudio-community/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MLX-4bit @0c4a20a6; our shards are byte-identical (sha256; = mlx-community/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit), so engines/lmstudio/farms holds a replica of that repo (4 small files downloaded, the rest symlinked) and nothing is copied. `lms load qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b --context-length 32768 --parallel 1`: parallel 1 for -np 1 parity; LM Studio's default (4) measured the same in a smoke (decode 87 vs 85 tok/s with thinking on, prefill 957/819 vs 951/844 tok/s, peak 25.3 GB both). Everything else is LM Studio's default. The MLX engine runs these vision checkpoints through its batched mlx-vlm path (BatchedVisionModelKit), which offers no speculative decoding: a draft model is refused ('not supported for batched vision models'; mlx-lm's draft speculation would also need trimmable caches, which the GatedDeltaNet layers' ArraysCache is not), mlx-vlm drops mtp.* weights (LM Studio's --speculative-draft-mtp is a llama.cpp/GGUF feature), and KV-cache quantization is not available on that path. Prompt cache: RAM plus LM Studio's default disk tier (unlinked temp file in /tmp). Thinking is switched off per request by reasoning_effort none, which LM Studio maps to the hub model's enableThinking custom field (chat_template_kwargs is ignored; without the hub model.yaml neither works). Usage is reported in the stream; cached prompt tokens are not. LM Studio stops at max_tokens-1 (511 of 512, checked by re-tokenizing the text), so every decode run carries a completion_tokens flag; rates use the reported count. Daemon pid from ~/.lmstudio/.internal/llmster-pid.lock: memory is the whole llmster tree (daemon + node worker hosting the engine). LM Studio's llama.cpp runtime (2.60.0 = llama.cpp b11698) is not the faster choice here: LM Studio's own GGUF of this model (lmstudio-community Q4_K_M, 21.2 GB) has no MTP layer (header: 40 blocks, no nextn tensors), i.e. plain llama.cpp, measured standalone (b11669, Q4_K_M) at 62.7 tok/s decode and 728/630 tok/s prefill; the 21 GB download would not fit the disk reserve.
